findings.quote: A corporation that makes independent political expenditures over $10,000 in a calendar year shall publicly disclose each person who contributed more than $1,000 toward those expenditures.
findings.mechanism: Corporations must track and report individual contributions over $1,000 when making significant independent political expenditures.

analysis.answer: Under current law, corporations making independent political expenditures only report the total amount spent, without disclosing funding sources. The measure changes this by requiring corporations that spend over $10,000 on such expenditures to publicly disclose any person who contributed more than $1,000 toward those expenditures.
Corporations will incur administrative and compliance costs to track donor identities, determine which funds are applied toward political expenditures, and file public disclosures.

Corporations bear the compliance costs. Voters, researchers, and opposing campaigns benefit from increased information regarding who funds political messaging. Individual donors who prefer to remain anonymous bear the loss of privacy.

Donors wishing to remain anonymous may reduce their contributions, give just under the $1,000 threshold, or route their money through other entities not subject to the same disclosure rules. Corporations might alter how they fund political expenditures to avoid triggering the disclosure requirement.

The measure addresses an information gap where the public does not know which individuals are funding corporate political spending. The mechanism mandates disclosure of large donors, though its effectiveness may depend on how easily funds can be traced or whether contributions can be routed through alternative channels.
